created_trees.objective: Demander un programme combinant les sources T1 et T4, en partant de la source la plus rapide T1. Mesurer et valider le résultat combiné sur le protocole officiel; ne pas supposer les gains additifs. Le comparer à T1, T4 et au baseline.
created_trees.stop_condition: Ne retenir l’intégration que si elle est valide et correcte et améliore le meilleur résultat selon le critère officiel; sinon conserver T1 comme source la plus rapide et ne pas poursuivre cette combinaison.
created_trees.subject: Mesurer l’intégration du parallélisme externe T1 et du SIMD T4

active_architecture.warning: Model wall times overlap research; do not add them to campaign wall time

decision.rationale: Lire le fichier source de Gm1 pour vérifier concrètement la fusion T1/T4 avant de choisir la prochaine intégration.

Prendre Gm1 comme base (valide, 0,037432 s, score 0,912627), qui conserve le parallélisme borné de T1 et les lots SIMD de huit voies de T4. Y intégrer les transformations distinctes des meilleurs essais mesurés de T2 (récurrence bilatérale pour les puissances terminales, 1dc5570ef1884777 : 0,296868 s) et T3 (coefficients de transition factorisés, 55e402f3863b4c72 : 0,294283 s). Ces deux programmes sont individuellement plus lents que Gm1; leurs mesures ne garantissent aucun gain combiné. Préserver les 64 exposants -64 à 62 par pas de deux, l’ordre de rollback et la tolérance; demander d’abord le contrôle de correction, puis comparer la mesure officielle à Gm1 sans présumer d’additivité.

decision.rationale: G (600ed5dcd12b4666) est valide et correct à 0,019241 s. Tester une optimisation locale de sa récurrence terminale, inspirée de la construction bilatérale T2 : avancer les chaînes de puissances positive et négative ensemble, en conservant l’ordre des multiplications de chaque chaîne et les exposants -64 à 62. La mesure doit établir si réduire le nombre de boucles SIMD améliore le programme complet.

Use the measured, correct G candidate 1e97ac568500465d (0.018706 s) as the base. Test the distinct rollback FMA formulation from the valid T3 trial 31c053d9f320458b. That trial was slower in isolation, so this tests whether explicit fusion interacts differently with G’s SIMD batches; do not assume a gain, and retain the existing traversal and endpoint convention.

Finish and request independent confirmation of the best measured candidate. Integration 83a1c1876f744ea3 was correct at 0.014417 s, faster than its parent 1e97ac568500465d at 0.018706 s. The promising recurrence, coefficient-hoisting, SIMD, and FMA ideas have been combined and evaluated; the remaining time does not support another integration plus confirmation. These are search measurements, not independent confirmation.

children.objective: In `src/candidate.cpp`, investigate parallelizing the independent per-element pricing work and dispatch using the supplied `threads` budget. Explore a low-overhead serial path for small workloads and suitable work partitioning without hardcoding the environment's 40-thread setting or changing global OpenMP controls. Preserve complete output overwrite and correctness for every entry. Compare whole-call timings across the official workload and available `n`/`threads` cases, including parallel overhead, and record failed scheduling or threshold variants.
children.subject: Outer-loop CPU parallelism and thread-budget-aware dispatch

children.objective: In `src/candidate.cpp`, focus only on generating terminal payoffs more cheaply than 64 repeated `powf` evaluations per input. Explore a recurrence or other general power-generation method while preserving all 64 terminal indices and their existing exponents `2*j-64` (`-64` through `62` by twos), the `max(0, X-S*upow)` floor, and the subsequent rollback. Validate varied inputs, especially values near payoff boundaries, against the fixed tolerance; record failed numerical variants and compare full-call timings.
children.subject: Reduce terminal-state power-function cost without changing endpoint convention

children.objective: In `src/candidate.cpp`, focus on the rollback transition expression: explore hoisting input-invariant factors (including discount-related division) or equivalent arithmetic rearrangements to reduce work repeated across the 2,080 state updates. Keep the backward `j`/`k` update order and endpoint convention; retain only variants that satisfy the fixed tolerance on varied inputs. Report accuracy and whole-call timing rather than assuming algebraic equivalence guarantees acceptable rounding or speed.
children.subject: Hoist invariant rollback coefficients and reduce per-state arithmetic

children.objective: In `src/candidate.cpp`, explore SIMD or batched execution across independent input elements (or another demonstrably distinct SIMD mapping) while leaving the baseline terminal-power generation and rollback arithmetic formulation unchanged, to avoid duplicating the other trees' subjects. Use only instructions/features supported by the actual compile target; available flags are not established here. Preserve every lane's output and correctness on varied inputs, and measure full-call performance including batching and scratch costs. Record ineffective or incorrect vectorization attempts.
children.subject: SIMD mapping across independent options

decision.rationale: Lire le fichier source de Gm1 pour vérifier concrètement la fusion T1/T4 avant de choisir la prochaine intégration.

Prendre Gm1 comme base (valide, 0,037432 s, score 0,912627), qui conserve le parallélisme borné de T1 et les lots SIMD de huit voies de T4. Y intégrer les transformations distinctes des meilleurs essais mesurés de T2 (récurrence bilatérale pour les puissances terminales, 1dc5570ef1884777 : 0,296868 s) et T3 (coefficients de transition factorisés, 55e402f3863b4c72 : 0,294283 s). Ces deux programmes sont individuellement plus lents que Gm1; leurs mesures ne garantissent aucun gain combiné. Préserver les 64 exposants -64 à 62 par pas de deux, l’ordre de rollback et la tolérance; demander d’abord le contrôle de correction, puis comparer la mesure officielle à Gm1 sans présumer d’additivité.

decision.rationale: G (600ed5dcd12b4666) est valide et correct à 0,019241 s. Tester une optimisation locale de sa récurrence terminale, inspirée de la construction bilatérale T2 : avancer les chaînes de puissances positive et négative ensemble, en conservant l’ordre des multiplications de chaque chaîne et les exposants -64 à 62. La mesure doit établir si réduire le nombre de boucles SIMD améliore le programme complet.

Use the measured, correct G candidate 1e97ac568500465d (0.018706 s) as the base. Test the distinct rollback FMA formulation from the valid T3 trial 31c053d9f320458b. That trial was slower in isolation, so this tests whether explicit fusion interacts differently with G’s SIMD batches; do not assume a gain, and retain the existing traversal and endpoint convention.

These are search measurements, not independent confirmation.

children.objective: In `src/candidate.cpp`, investigate parallelizing the independent per-element pricing work and dispatch using the supplied `threads` budget. Explore a low-overhead serial path for small workloads and suitable work partitioning without hardcoding the environment's 40-thread setting or changing global OpenMP controls. Preserve complete output overwrite and correctness for every entry. Compare whole-call timings across the official workload and available `n`/`threads` cases, including parallel overhead, and record failed scheduling or threshold variants.
children.subject: Outer-loop CPU parallelism and thread-budget-aware dispatch

children.objective: In `src/candidate.cpp`, focus only on generating terminal payoffs more cheaply than 64 repeated `powf` evaluations per input. Explore a recurrence or other general power-generation method while preserving all 64 terminal indices and their existing exponents `2*j-64` (`-64` through `62` by twos), the `max(0, X-S*upow)` floor, and the subsequent rollback. Validate varied inputs, especially values near payoff boundaries, against the fixed tolerance; record failed numerical variants and compare full-call timings.
children.subject: Reduce terminal-state power-function cost without changing endpoint convention

children.objective: In `src/candidate.cpp`, focus on the rollback transition expression: explore hoisting input-invariant factors (including discount-related division) or equivalent arithmetic rearrangements to reduce work repeated across the 2,080 state updates. Keep the backward `j`/`k` update order and endpoint convention; retain only variants that satisfy the fixed tolerance on varied inputs. Report accuracy and whole-call timing rather than assuming algebraic equivalence guarantees acceptable rounding or speed.
children.subject: Hoist invariant rollback coefficients and reduce per-state arithmetic

children.objective: In `src/candidate.cpp`, explore SIMD or batched execution across independent input elements (or another demonstrably distinct SIMD mapping) while leaving the baseline terminal-power generation and rollback arithmetic formulation unchanged, to avoid duplicating the other trees' subjects. Use only instructions/features supported by the actual compile target; available flags are not established here. Preserve every lane's output and correctness on varied inputs, and measure full-call performance including batching and scratch costs. Record ineffective or incorrect vectorization attempts.
children.subject: SIMD mapping across independent options
